verdicts.quote: an assigned user opens a "Grok Bot" entry from the Lightning App Launcher and sees a chat panel ... no other entry point (record pages, mobile app, Experience Cloud) is in scope.
Sharing, object CRUD and field-level security are not applicable because the product reads and writes no org records (recorded as an exclusion with this reason
Sharing, object CRUD and field-level security are not applicable because the product reads and writes no org records
only users granted the access grant (a permission set deployed with the product) can open the panel and invoke the server-side operation
verdicts.missing: Administration (configuring, entering the key, assigning the grant) is given only to an 'Org admin' actor, not to a named permission set or equivalent; who assigns the grant is left open (G-6).

verdicts.quote: context lives only in the open panel (browser memory); reload, navigating away or closing the tab ends it; nothing is stored in the org (see R-8).
Apex makes a single synchronous HTTP callout to xAI and returns a DTO ... No queue, Continuation or middle tier.
verdicts.missing: The callout-after-DML rule appears only in Evidence limits, not as a design constraint; the design is synchronous rather than asynchronous, and the long-running-request concern is left to a probe.

verdicts.quote: the xAI API key exists only in the org's secret-credential facility (AD-3): never in source, metadata files, custom settings, the browser, Apex return values, debug logs or the transcript.
the callout waits at most 60 seconds (Timeout_Seconds). The bot makes exactly one callout per submission (platform ceiling: 100 callouts per transaction, 120 s cumulative).
verdicts.missing: CPU time limit is not named; heap is stated (NFR-5, 10 MB), but the CPU time ceiling is not given.

verdicts.quote: Apex tests with `HttpCalloutMock` capturing the request (remote tests, TAP reporter, run in the org)
a Named Credential pointing at the xAI base URL with a custom header `Authorization: Bearer <key>` (formula header; key never in the URL)
A Lightning web component chat panel calls one Apex `@AuraEnabled` operation imperatively; Apex makes a single synchronous HTTP callout to xAI and returns a DTO
verdicts.missing: The interface relies on the call returning inline; no async notification mechanism (platform event, polling, LMS) is specified, and whether inline return holds under long-running request limits is left to a probe.

verdicts.quote: retry is user-initiated, duplicates are possible and accepted (no idempotency key; stated in the timeout message).
verdicts.missing: No idempotency on the request or message; duplicate processing is explicitly accepted rather than prevented.

verdicts.quote: revisit only if concurrent long-running request limits bite (a documented note says callout time is not counted toward the 5 s long-running threshold; confirm by probe).
verdicts.missing: The concurrent-request limit value and what the user sees when a request is refused because of it are not stated.

verdicts.quote: auth | xAI HTTP 401 or 403 ... upstream | xAI HTTP 5xx | "Grok is unavailable (error <status>). Try again." | timeout | no response within Timeout_Seconds (60 s)
rate-limited | xAI HTTP 429 | "Grok is rate-limited right now. Wait a moment and try again." ... no automatic retry
a reply cut off by the cap is shown with the visible note "Reply was cut off at the length limit" ... A reply arriving at 60 s or later is not shown (R-7 timeout).
D-persist no conversation persistence (R-3, R-8); basis: request asks for no history, avoids personal-data storage; alternative: custom object per user
verdicts.missing: No stored shape; the in-memory transcript has role and failed status, but timestamps, model identifier and token/usage counts are not recorded anywhere.

verdicts.quote: Chat content is not stored in the org and not written to logs
No Salesforce record data is read or sent; only text the user types and the configured system instruction leave the org.
keep at most 20 messages (Max_History_Messages, including the new message) and at most 100,000 characters total (Max_Context_Chars); drop the oldest whole exchange repeatedly until both hold
the trimmed message must be 1..Max_Message_Chars characters ... Max_Message_Chars = 4,000. Exactly 4,000 accepted; 4,001 rejected.
these values are deployed with the product as configuration and changed without code change: model id, system instruction
verdicts.missing: No explicit admin off switch; failed requests are visible only as debug-log lines (NFR-7), and there is no admin view of failures.

verdicts.quote: A persistent audit/log object is excluded: a development org used by one or a few admins, and content logging would conflict with R-8.
verdicts.missing: No record of who asked what and what was answered; only an outcome-class debug line, with no stated retention.

verdicts.quote: the product deploys additively to the chosen dev org with the Salesforce CLI
verdicts.missing: How configuration and credential differ between dev and production, and the production code-coverage requirement (NFR-8 defers to the org's effective test level, read at plan).

verdicts.quote: no numeric Grok latency target is invented (not controllable). Bound: Timeout_Seconds = 60 (B-5); observable: pending state is visible from the moment of submit until the call settles
States designed: empty (short greeting with three example prompts), loading (pending indicator, R-11), error (inline, Retry, R-7), not-configured, denied; trimmed-context divider.
it adds only its own components (tab, app or tab-in-existing-app, permission set, Apex, web component, configuration, credential shell) and changes no existing org metadata.
